facts.text: Nagytétény Castle, a late Baroque mansion, exemplifies the Grassalkovich style that flourished in Hungary during the 18th century.
The Museum of Applied Arts in Nagytétény was housed in the former Száraz‑Rudnyánszky mansion, a landmark of Hungarian late Baroque architecture.
Since 2010, the museum’s entrance hall has been restored, and a 2011 reconstruction plan preserved its historic façade.
The museum’s collections span ceramics, glass, contemporary design, and metalwork, offering a comprehensive view of applied arts.
Virtual tours of the Nagytétény mansion allow visitors to explore its interior without leaving their car.
The museum participates in the Danube Interreg project, aiming to strengthen cultural identity across the Danube region.
